URL: https://www.reuters.com/world/uk/bank-england-rate-setters-warn-sparks-tinderbox-2026-09-24/
Reuters — published Thursday 24 September 2026 16:44 BST (15:44 UTC), updated 17:19 BST. By David Milliken and Andy Bruce; writing William Schomberg.

HEADLINE: Two Bank of England deputy governors signalled they are moving closer to voting for a RATE RISE, as high energy costs risk entrenching inflation.

FACTS (Reuters):
- Deputy Governors Clare Lombardelli and Sarah Breeden, who both voted to hold Bank Rate at 3.75% last week, said they were considering shifting position.
- Markets are pricing a 75% chance of a quarter-point rise at the next MPC meeting in November; another hike fully priced by February.
- The BoE has not followed the US Federal Reserve and the ECB, which have raised rates, but warned last week it might if the Iran war drags on. It forecasts UK inflation topping 4% early next year, more than double the 2% target.
- Swati Dhingra sounded a less urgent note, saying the extent of long-term inflation pressure from the Iran war would become clearer over the winter; Britain is not seeing the kind of broad-based price rises of 2022 and the jobs market is now weaker.
- Governor Andrew Bailey is due to speak publicly on Friday 25 September. (FORWARD-LOOKING DIARY CLAIM — sourced to Reuters, single source.)

QUOTES:
Sarah Breeden, BoE Deputy Governor, to the London Macro Policy Forum organised by the National Institute of Economic and Social Research (Reuters): "The more sparks we're throwing in the tinderbox, the more likely we might have to turn the hose on it."
Clare Lombardelli, BoE Deputy Governor, in a speech in Warsaw (Reuters): "The longer higher energy prices persist, the greater the risk that indirect effects build and that inflation expectations, wage bargaining and price-setting behaviour begin to adjust in response."
Andrew Bailey, BoE Governor, last week (quoted by Reuters): "the longer this goes on, the more difficult this becomes" — on the rise in energy prices.
Investec analysts (Reuters): "Unless there is material progress in negotiations that see substantial energy flows resume transit through the Strait of Hormuz, we imagine that tolerance for the majority of committee members will soon run thin, triggering a 25bp rate hike, likely in November."

HOUSEHOLD ANGLE: mortgage rates. A November hike would raise tracker and new fixed-rate mortgage costs; savers gain. Bank Rate currently 3.75%.
